title: GPU region sync — weekly digest and action ledger
content:
Meeting: GPU Region Sync — weekly digest
Date: 2027-09-07
Time: 09:30 PT (30m) — cadence: weekly
Facilitator: Priya Shah
Attendees: Priya, Liam, Xinyi, Diego, Asha, Ben, SRE oncall (Carlos)

One-line summary:
This week we focused on cross-region prewarm coordination, reviewed an A/B test for instance prewarming, updated regional capacity hedges for EU-West and APAC, and captured three unblockers for Dedicated allocation.

Standup snapshot (quick bullets):
- EU-West utilization: 76% steady; 4-hour tail of small spikes on 09-05 coincident with model release A (model-v2.3).
- APAC utilization: 89% daytime; observed elevated cold-start latency in tokyo-1 during the 02:00–05:00 PT window.
- US-West: capacity margin at 22% after recent burst reservations, nominal.
- Prewarming experiment (see experiment notes below) shows 18% median P95 latency reduction for chat workloads when prefix warmers are used for sequences > 512 tokens.

Events and anomalies:
- 09-05 model-v2.3 rollout caused a transient KV cache eviction pattern that increased average warmup time by +40ms for the first two minutes after deploy. Root cause: memory layout change in attention layer requiring kernel fallback. Assigned INF-3499 to runtime team.
- Tokyo-1 cold start root: new host image (img-2027-08-31) missed a startup hook that restores shared cache blobs. Hotfix applied 09-06; verified by smoke tests.
- Brief preemption in EU-West (preemptible nodes) triggered a fallback to reserved capacity but did not breach SLOs. Noted for prioritization logic tuning.

Capacity pulse (numbers are approximations from Friday 23:00 UTC snapshot):
- Global total GPUs: 8,760 (all regions)
- Usable (non-preemptible committed): 6,420
- Reserved for Dedicated: 1,300
- Free buffer (elastic pool): ~1,040 (12% of usable)
- Hot-standby primed pools: us-west-1: 120 GPUs, eu-west-1: 60 GPUs, apac-tokyo-1: 30 GPUs

Decisions made:
- Increase EU-West hot-standby by +20 GPUs for the next 72 hours to hedge against anticipated enterprise traffic spike (customer X ramp). Owner: Liam. Due: 2027-09-09.
- Keep APAC prewarming schedule at current cadence but add an overnight warm pass between 00:30–02:30 PT to address cold-start window. Owner: Xinyi. Due: 2027-09-08.
- Pause further capacity reclamation on us-central until we confirm no further churn from legacy backfills. Owner: Diego. Due: 2027-09-10.

Experiment notes — "prefix priming" A/B (INF-3421):
- Hypothesis: proactive KV prefix warmers seeded with recent popular prefixes reduce token generation P95 for long sequences.
- Sample: chat workload traffic tagged "prod-chat"; 72-hour run; cohorts: 50% control, 50% primed.
- Results: median P95 decrease 18%, 95th P99 unchanged (noise). Cost: small increase in idle GPU-minutes (~ +3.2%) for primed cohort.
- Observations: benefit concentrated on sequences >512 tokens and sessions with higher token churn. No measurable improvement for short queries (<128 tokens).
- Action: rollout priming to select Dedicated pools and run another 1-week validate for enterprise traffic patterns. Owner: Asha. JIRA: INF-3421.

Cross-team blockers / dependencies:
- Runtime team needs to commit a small kernel fallback patch to avoid KV eviction pattern on model-v2.x family (PR linked in artifacts). Blocker prevents safe scaling of prewarming for that family. Blocker owner: Ben (runtime liaison).
- Network team investigating intermittent RPS drops in apac-tokyo-1 peering; impacts prewarm health checks (ticket created).

Operational runbook changes proposed:
- Add a dedicated prewarm health metric: prewarm-hit-rate (ratio of requests served with warmed KV) surfaced in Console under infra -> region priming. Owner: Priya.
- Add automated rollback rule: if primed cohort shows >5% increase in P99 latency across 10m window, auto-disable priming. Owner: SRE automation (Carlos).

Action items (owner and due dates):
- Liam: provision +20 EU-West hot-standby GPUs and confirm placement by 2027-09-09.
- Xinyi: schedule overnight warm pass in APAC and validate cold-start window improvement by 2027-09-08.
- Asha: run 1-week validate of priming on Dedicated traffic and surface cost delta to finance by 2027-09-15.
- Ben: land kernel fallback patch and link PR to INF-3499 by 2027-09-12.
- Diego: freeze reclamation on us-central and update capacity ledger by 2027-09-10.
- Priya: author a short Console doc page for prewarm-hit-rate and submit for review by 2027-09-11.

Follow-ups for next sync:
- Report back on priming validate (Asha) and whether cost delta justifies wider rollout.
- Runtime patch status (Ben) and any perf regressions.
- APAC warm pass verification (Xinyi) and additional network observations.

Appendix — quick telemetry snippets (09-07 06:00 UTC snapshot):
- EU-West average queue depth: 3.4 requests per GPU; P95 token latency for long chat: 310ms (primed: 255ms).
- APAC cold-start incidents (last 7 days): 7 incidents; mean MTTR: 13m (after image-hook hotfix reduced from 28m).
- Cost note: priming idle GPU-hours impact estimated at +0.9k GPU-hours/month for current scale (finance tagged for review).

Notes / freeform thoughts:
- Consider a small catalog of "warm profiles" per workload class (short-chat, long-chat, llm-batch) so primers are less noisy and cheaper.
- We should start tracking model-architectural changes (e.g., attention memory layout) as a signal in deployment pipelines; runtime can subscribe and trigger limited canaries when layout changes are detected.

References: linked Jira tickets and Confluence playbook above.

End of digest.
